name: Agreement with the Tonkawa, October 21, 1891, ratified March 3, 1893, ceding the former Nez Perce (Joseph's band) tract in the Cherokee Outlet
citation: Act of March 3, 1893, ch. 209, sec. 11, 27 Stat. 612, 643
nations: Nimiipuu (Nez Perce), Joseph's band, former occupants
promises: Royce records that the tract, Area 606, had been conveyed by the Cherokee Nation to the United States in trust for the Nez Perce by deed of June 14, 1883 (Royce, p. 947).

The Indian Claims Commission records that Joseph's band, removed from Fort Leavenworth under the Act of May 27, 1878, was settled on this tract of 90,710.89 acres, and that it was transferred to the Tonkawa in June 1885 after the Nez Perce were moved elsewhere (Cherokee Docket 173, finding 5).
By the 1891 agreement the Tonkawa ceded the four townships to the United States, and the 1893 Act appropriated $30,600 to pay them, part to be held in the Treasury at 5 percent (27 Stat. 643).
landTaken: Four townships, given by the Act as ninety thousand seven hundred and ten and eighty-nine one-hundredths acres, ceded by the Tonkawa (27 Stat. 643).

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule pp. 946-947
Act of March 3, 1893, ch. 209, 27 Stat. 612 (Indian appropriations, fiscal 1894)
Cherokee Nation v. United States, Docket 173, Findings of Fact (9 Ind. Cl. Comm. 162, April 3, 1961)
sources.publisher: Indian Claims Commission Decisions, Oklahoma State University Library

openQuestions: treaties.json names this row for Nez Perce (Joseph's band) and the Nez Perce Tribe of Idaho. Royce's 1893 entry for Area 606 is the Tonkawa agreement of October 21, 1891 (27 Stat. 643); the Nez Perce had left the tract in 1885. The present-day party to this cession is the Tonkawa Tribe of Oklahoma. Not edited.
No Indian Claims Commission or Court of Claims decision on the Tonkawa's price for this tract was found (ICC title and full-text searches for Tonkawa return only Texas aboriginal claims).

The Joseph band's own claims, including any for its time in Indian Territory, were in ICC Docket 186, settled in 1974 (see cession-1873-06-16-nez-perc); whether they reached this tract was not checked.
The Tonkawa Tribe's own account was not located.
